source.section: Number of Factors and Sum of all Factors

problem.text: What is the sum of the factors of $140$?

steps.title: Where to start: prime factorize $140$
steps.body: Listing all the factors and adding them works, but it is easy to miss one. Every factor is built from the primes of $140$, so the prime factorization tells us exactly what the factors are.

your_turn.prompt: Write $140$ as a product of prime powers.

steps.title: Use the sum-of-divisors formula
steps.body:
Every factor has the form $2^a\cdot 5^b\cdot 7^c$ with $0\le a\le 2$, $0\le b\le 1$, $0\le c\le 1$. Multiplying out the product below picks one term from each bracket in every possible way, so it produces each factor exactly once.
$$(1 + 2 + 2^2)(1 + 5)(1 + 7)$$

your_turn.prompt: What is the value of each bracket?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The sum of the factors is $7\cdot 6\cdot 8 = 336$. The answer is **336**.

verification.verifier_notes: Independent reviewer re-derived the answer, checked the text against the book image, and found no holes.
